scope: 21 whole exclusions, all fields read; original repeated scope boilerplate inspected once as byte-identical and corrected explicitly in each proposed record. Exact final integration remains pending.
source_scope_basis: source-scope-disposition.v3.json and frozen evaluation-policy.v4.json; page 129 was previously rendered and bound in scope disposition.

rows.review_disposition: Full 1 supports a brief royal-touch detail within sacred kingship, not an independently developed medical subject. Retain the ritual’s political meaning in its parent and correct global scope language.

Full 20 confirms named large factories as exceptions to small-workshop organization. Accept local exclusion of separate enterprise biographies while preserving scale, discipline, guild freedom and suspicion in industrial organization; Réveillon’s later political role remains eligible.

Full 42 supports fortunes/pensions as evidence of real patronage rewards. The numbers and separate biographies may be subordinate, but do not remove the mechanism of favour producing wealth and political influence.
Full 44 gives brief Herder/Alfieri examples of a still-limited cultural backlash. Retain the backlash and their illustrative routes if useful; later developed treatments remain unaffected.

Full 47 supports subscription figures as comparative affordability evidence. They do not require an independent numerical subject; preserve cost limiting access and shared-reading institutions reducing it.

Full 46–47 confirms illustrative locations, but reading rooms, literary societies and academies have distinct functions and accessibility. Exclude only individual microheadings, not these institutional differences.

Full 67–68 supports substantive fiscal continuity: taxes and overridden objections enabled new loans after Necker. A separate Joly biography is optional, but the causal tax/credit phase must remain in the war-finance parent. Duplicate incidental/principal summaries may be consolidated without dropping the action.

Full 77–78 confirms Young as witness to opinion in these passages. Attribution-only personal exclusion is acceptable here, but the quoted Dutch focus, distrust and their source role remain eligible, and Young’s separately developed observation role elsewhere is unaffected.

Full 73 supports a brief ministerial-transition episode. Correct the evidence’s unqualified motive to the source’s ostensibly failing to support Calonne; keep Lamoignon’s replacement and the sequence before Calonne’s dismissal in the ministerial account.
Full 101 supports costume as brief visual differentiation of orders. No separate costume subject is required; retain the distinction within the ceremonial/institutional scene where useful.

Full 103 gives royal grief and ministerial paralysis a specific short-term causal role. Excluding a separate dynastic death heading is reasonable only while that causal context survives; do not dismiss the entire sentence as nonindexable.

Full 87 and 105 confirm Dorset as a quoted diplomatic observer rather than a developed actor. Preserve the poverty and sovereignty arguments and attribution, without manufacturing biography from quotation.

Full 115 develops Quincey as a rumour catalyst in escalating rural attacks. Separate local weighting is optional, but the causal spread of an assumed aristocratic plot must remain under fear/anti-seigneurial violence; revise rhetoric that could erase it as merely decorative.

Full 113 confirms brief distinct city examples within municipal revolution. Exclude default separate city units here, while retaining differences among riot, grain/machinery attacks and troop refusal in the broader mobilization treatment.

The 129 numbered key is an excluded graphic/navigation region under the frozen policy. Retain the caption only as eligible descriptive text; remove any implication that only separate name weighting is excluded while interior semantics remain usable.

Full 137 supports Gerle’s motion as a substantive religious-polarization episode but little personal development. Retain the motion under religious settlement and the 137/142 date conflict; exclusion of separate biography does not exclude the argument.

Full 143 supports Expilly as an illustrative first episcopal-election conflict. Preserve refusal of confirmation and the resulting impossibility of a peaceful transition, without requiring a separate biographical unit.

Full 151 supports Drouet’s dash to Varennes and attributes his identification claim. Preserve local action in the failed escape; separate biography is optional, and wording must not erase the distinction between recognition and his claim to have made it.
Full 160 confirms a compact list of German reactions with skeptical exceptions. Personal units are not required, but the contrast between enthusiasm and skepticism remains part of European reception.
Full 160–161 confirms Kellgren and Stroganov as brief attributed celebrants. Preserve the reach and content of enthusiasm without creating biographies from single quotations.

Full 168 makes Pitt’s election victory contextual to flagging reform before Burke’s intervention. This local exclusion cannot remove his substantive wartime, domestic or diplomatic treatment elsewhere.
